subject.title: Enforce a changed-file TypeScript LOC growth ratchet

question: Should TypeScript physical-line growth become a mandatory merge-blocking invariant for changed production files, using the proposed 500-line and no-growth rules?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but choosing a hard merge policy, its exclusions, and treatment of legacy oversized files affects every TypeScript contribution and must be explicitly owned.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow ratchet
options.body: Implement the baseline-free changed-file gate with shared selection logic and focused regression coverage across local and CI entry points.

options.title: Keep advisory reporting
options.body: Report changed-file LOC growth without blocking merges while maintainers gather false-positive and contributor-friction data.

options.title: Decline LOC enforcement
options.body: Retain the 500-line guidance as a review convention rather than adding a mechanical merge gate.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow ratchet
recommendation.body: Implement the baseline-free changed-file gate with shared selection logic and focused regression coverage across local and CI entry points.

likelyOwner.reason: The changed-check graph and recent check infrastructure appear to be primarily owned by steipete, who also opened this focused proposal.
